# Single source of experiment configuration. Every run records the resolved config in its manifest.
seed: 13

dataset:
  name: iu_xray
  raw_dir: data/raw/iu_xray
  interim: data/interim/iu_xray/documents.jsonl
  splits: {pilot: round1, heldout: round2}   # round1=12, round2=38
  # Dataset-agnostic by design: adding NLM-Chem/NLM-Gene/SciERC = new ingest adapter only.

label_map:
  "Anatomy": ANAT
  "Observation: Definite Present": OBS-DP
  "Observation: Definite Absent": OBS-DA
  "Observation: Uncertain": OBS-U

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Research program (three goals). Stages are gated so one codebase serves all.
#   goal1: guidelines as alignment mechanism (ACL 2026 - reuse/refine EXISTING)
#   goal2: induce guidelines when none exist (CURRENT)
#          ACL 2026 Limitations: "assumes the availability of an initial human-written
#          guideline... Addressing this limitation will require methods for guideline generation."
#   goal3: framework to evaluate guideline quality
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
goal: goal2
guideline:
  provider: schema_only   # schema_only | induced (artifact from `induce`) | existing(goal1)
                          # | minimal_feedback(goal2b) | patched
  # D26/D27/D31 evidence budget. Selection is MATHEMATICALLY defined, not a magic count (rule 2):
  #   coverage: per label, minimal most-frequent mention prefix whose cumulative gold-span count
  #     >= coverage_tau * (label total). tau=1.0 => all mentions. Deterministic, per-label adaptive.
  # coverage_tau is the SWEPT axis (D31: {0.5,0.7,0.9,1.0}); 0.9 is the primary artifact.
  # examples_per_mention fixed at 1 = minimal grounding (one witnessing sentence); swept only if
  #   the tau sweep shows the artifact is example-count sensitive.
  evidence:
    selection: coverage
    coverage_tau: 0.9
    ranking: frequency        # frequency | doc_frequency (D32: compared, not assumed)
    examples_per_mention: 1

# D19/D21: single model runs the WHOLE induction loop (annotate -> edit -> annotate).
# No separate editor: the loop is self-contained per model, so fixed-editor self-alignment
# does not arise. D20: the produced guideline is then evaluated on OTHER models (transfer),
# which is the evidence that the artifact is a guideline and not an optimized prompt.
annotate:
  induction:
    mode: self_loop       # self_loop (D19) | fixed_editor (superseded)
    reasoning: true       # ACL H2: reasoning needed (deductive apply + inductive refine)
  annotators:
    # D22: frontier tier, 4 independent families.
    # IDs verified against each account 2026-07-15 (`gstudy models` / google-genai models.list).
    # gpt pinned to the dated snapshot (D22: 5.4->5.5 drift is our pinning argument).
    # google exposes no stable gemini-3.1-pro on this account -- only the -preview alias.
    closed:
      - {id: gpt, family: openai, model: gpt-5.5-2026-04-23}
      - {id: gemini, family: google, model: gemini-3.1-pro-preview}
      - {id: deepseek, family: deepseek, model: deepseek-v4-pro}   # or deepseek-v4-flash
      - {id: claude, family: anthropic, model: claude-opus-4-8}    # no dated alias exposed
    open_weight:
      - {id: ow_low, tier: low, family: meta, model: TBD, note: "~8B weak anchor"}
      - {id: ow_low_mid, tier: low_mid, family: alibaba, model: TBD, note: "~12-14B"}
      - {id: ow_mid, tier: mid, family: mistral, model: TBD, note: "~24B independent lineage"}
      - {id: ow_mid_high, tier: mid_high, family: google, model: TBD, note: "~27-32B long ctx"}
      - {id: ow_high, tier: high, family: deepseek, model: TBD, note: "near-frontier MoE"}
  # D34: temperature is NOT sent to the API. Reasoning models (gpt-5.x, o-series) reject an
  # explicit temperature, so "use each model's default" is the only uniform policy across the
  # pool. Trade-off: greedy determinism is lost (was temp=0 for deepseek); accepted for a
  # confound-free, no-branch cross-model comparison. This key is retained for provenance only.
  decoding: {temperature: unset}
  backend: mock           # mock | openai | deepseek (OpenAI-compatible) | local_vllm (TBD)
  requirements:
    min_context_tokens: 32000
    require_json: true
  track_parse_errors: true
  pin_weights: true
  screening:
    # Motivated by ACL 2026 4.3: prior work EXCLUDED smaller local models
    # ("unsatisfactory baseline, unstable adherence, no consistent gains after moderation").
    # We screen explicitly and REPORT exclusions -- locating the capability floor is a finding.
    enabled: true
    report_excluded: true
    checks:
      context_fit: {required: true}
      json_validity: {min_valid_rate: 0.90}
      schema_only_floor: {min_f1: 0.05}

evaluate:
  extrinsic: {metric: exact_span_type_micro_f1}
  transfer_eval: {enabled: true}   # D20: run each induced guideline on the OTHER models
  intrinsic: {enabled: false}   # goal3 hook: guideline-document quality (expert/author validation)

discrepancy: {enabled: false}
feedback: {enabled: false, mode: rule_confirm}   # rule_confirm | case_label | gold_oracle
update: {enabled: false}

payload:
# RadGraph Reference-Entity Rerun

This directory contains a reference-entity relation diagnostic using the local RadGraph DyGIE++ checkpoint at `${USER_HOME}\Downloads\radgraph\models\model_checkpoint\model.tar.gz`.

## Definition

Human entity spans are forced through DyGIE++'s existing `gold_beam` path. The original encoder and trained relation head then predict directed relation labels. Human relation labels are absent from inference input and are used only after inference for evaluation.

All trained parameters are held fixed, but this is not a pure candidate-span-only intervention. The existing `gold_beam` implementation assigns a mention score of zero to every selected reference entity; the relation module adds those mention scores to its non-null relation logits. The diagnostic therefore changes both candidate availability and this deterministic mention-score term. Paper-facing text calls it a **reference-entity diagnostic**, not an oracle or a causal decomposition of entity versus relation error.

This differs from the matched-endpoint conditional diagnostic: the rerun evaluates all 1,454 human reference relations after supplying all 1,988 human reference entity spans, including entities the end-to-end model failed to detect. It is not described as a gold-standard oracle because the annotations were not independently adjudicated.

## Implementation

- `dygiepp_oracle/dygie/models/relation.py` enables the existing generic `gold_beam` pruner and accepts human NER labels as its span-selection mask.
- `dygiepp_oracle/dygie/models/dygie.py` passes NER labels to the relation module.
- No checkpoint parameter, relation scorer, or relation threshold was changed.
- `scripts/prepare_radgraph_oracle_input.py` converts character spans to the checkpoint's one-sentence token indices and rejects spans wider than the configured maximum of eight tokens.
- `scripts/run_legacy_allennlp.py` handles a Windows DLL load-order issue in the isolated Python 3.7 runtime.
- `scripts/evaluate_radgraph_oracle.py` normalizes predictions to human entity IDs and computes document-bootstrap confidence intervals.

## Primary result

Across 50 documents, the relation head predicts 1,319 relations and obtains micro-precision 0.711, recall 0.645, and F1 0.677 (95% document-bootstrap CI 0.643-0.711).

## Tokenization sensitivity

Two of 1,988 human entities end inside a token produced by the released inference tokenizer: `silhouette` within `silhouette;` and `patient` within `patient's`. Two variants were therefore evaluated:

1. exact-boundary tokenization, separating semicolon and apostrophe punctuation;
2. the released tokenizer unchanged, expanding only those two gold spans to its token boundaries.

Both variants produce identical relation predictions and identical evaluation counts. The exact-boundary output is the primary result; the released-tokenizer files provide the sensitivity check.

## Principal files

The existing filenames retain the legacy words `gold` and `oracle` so that recorded commands and checksums remain reproducible; paper-facing terminology is **human reference annotations** and **reference-entity rerun**.

- `oracle_gold_entities_50.jsonl`: exact-boundary inference input.
- `oracle_raw_50.jsonl`: raw DyGIE++ output.
- `oracle_relations_50.jsonl`: predictions normalized to human entity IDs.
- `oracle_evaluation.json`: primary results and bootstrap intervals.
- Files ending in `_released_tokenizer` contain the sensitivity variant.

"""Document-level bootstrap CIs for the headline comparisons (D29). No API calls -- pure recompute.

Why document-level and not span-level: spans within a report are not independent (one radiologist,
one style, repeated mentions), so resampling spans would understate the interval. The document is the
independent unit, so we resample documents with replacement and recompute micro-F1 from the stored
per-document tp/fp/fn. This is the standard NLP bootstrap and it is what an R&E reviewer will ask for.

Paired comparisons resample the SAME document indices for both conditions, which removes
document-difficulty from the difference and is the right test for "does A beat B on this test set".
It answers a different question from D39's induction variance (which is about the method, not the
test set) -- both belong in the paper.

Usage: python scripts/bootstrap_ci.py [--iters 10000]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import random
import re
import statistics as st
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
ITERS = 10000
SEED = 13


def f1_from(counts) -> float:
    tp = sum(c[0] for c in counts); fp = sum(c[1] for c in counts); fn = sum(c[2] for c in counts)
    p = tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else 0.0
    r = tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn else 0.0
    return 2 * p * r / (p + r) if p + r else 0.0


def load_counts(run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int, int]]:
    out = {}
    for line in (run_dir / "predictions.jsonl").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        r = json.loads(line)
        m = r["doc_metrics"]
        out[r["doc_id"]] = (m["tp"], m["fp"], m["fn"])
    return out


def boot_ci(counts: dict, iters: int, rng: random.Random) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    ids = list(counts)
    point = f1_from([counts[i] for i in ids])
    draws = []
    for _ in range(iters):
        s = [counts[rng.choice(ids)] for _ in ids]
        draws.append(f1_from(s))
    draws.sort()
    return point, draws[int(0.025 * iters)], draws[int(0.975 * iters)]


def boot_paired(a: dict, b: dict, iters: int, rng: random.Random) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
    ids = sorted(set(a) & set(b))
    # Guard, because the silent version of this bug already bit: if the two runs are on different
    # splits their doc ids are disjoint, the intersection is empty, and f1_from([]) returns 0.0 for
    # both sides -- yielding a confident-looking "+0.000, CI [0,0]" instead of an error.
    if not ids or len(ids) != len(a) or len(ids) != len(b):
        raise ValueError(f"paired runs do not cover the same documents: "
                         f"|A|={len(a)} |B|={len(b)} |A&B|={len(ids)}")
    diff = f1_from([a[i] for i in ids]) - f1_from([b[i] for i in ids])
    draws = []
    for _ in range(iters):
        s = [rng.choice(ids) for _ in ids]
        draws.append(f1_from([a[i] for i in s]) - f1_from([b[i] for i in s]))
    draws.sort()
    lo, hi = draws[int(0.025 * iters)], draws[int(0.975 * iters)]
    p = 2 * min(sum(1 for d in draws if d <= 0), sum(1 for d in draws if d >= 0)) / iters
    return diff, lo, hi, min(p, 1.0)


def find_runs() -> dict[str, list[Path]]:
    """Group finished heldout runs by condition, keeping the run dirs.

    Classification is delegated to gstudy.arms -- never re-derived here. Hand-rolled versions of this
    in five scripts produced four different cross-corpus mix-ups, including a MIMIC-induced guideline
    that was actually evaluated on IU (run 20260717T085636Z) and would otherwise be pooled into the
    IU tau=0.9 arm by this very function. arms.canonical() also forces the caller to state the corpus,
    so it cannot be forgotten.
    """
    from gstudy import arms
    prov = {}
    for g in (ROOT / "runs").glob("*induce_evidence*/guideline.json"):
        p = json.loads(g.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("provenance") or {}
        prov[g.parent.name.lower()] = p
    out: dict[str, list[Path]] = {}
    for m in sorted((ROOT / "runs").glob("*/manifest.json")):
        d = json.loads(m.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        met = d.get("metrics") or {}
        cfg = d.get("config") or {}
        be = str(cfg.get("annotate", {}).get("backend", ""))
        if d.get("stage") != "run_linear" or met.get("f1") is None or be.startswith("mock"):
            continue
        if not (m.parent / "predictions.jsonl").exists():
            continue
        interim = str((cfg.get("dataset") or {}).get("interim", "")).lower()
        corpus = "MIMIC" if "interim/radgraph" in interim.replace("\\", "/") else "IU"
        notes = d.get("notes") or ""
        # Held-out only, and at FULL size. Without this, pilot smoke runs (2 or 12 docs) and
        # truncated --limit runs get pooled into a condition and can win the median-draw pick.
        sp = [t.split("=")[1] for t in notes.split() if t.startswith("split=")]
        if (sp and sp[0] != "heldout") or met.get("n_docs") != (50 if corpus == "MIMIC" else 38):
            continue
        gf = [t.split("=", 1)[1] for t in notes.split() if t.startswith("guideline_file=")]
        if not gf:
            key = f"{corpus}:schema_only"
        else:
            g = gf[0].replace("\\", "/").lower()
            if "human_guidelines" in g:
                key = f"{corpus}:human:" + g.split("/")[-1].replace(".json", "")
            elif "ablation" in g:
                key = f"{corpus}:" + g.split("/")[-1].replace(".json", "")
            else:
                mm = re.search(r"(\d{8}t\d{6}z_induce_evidence_\w+)", g)
                pv = prov.get(mm.group(1)) if mm else None
                if not pv:
                    continue
                a = arms.arm_of(pv, ROOT)
                # The guideline's OWN corpus must match the corpus it was scored on. Without this a
                # MIMIC-induced guideline evaluated on IU lands in the IU arm and looks like a draw.
                if a is None or a["corpus"] != corpus:
                    continue
                if a["tau"] != 0.9 or a["negative_evidence"] or a["n"] != 12 \
                        or a["seed"] != 13 or a["ranking"] != "frequency":
                    continue
                key = (f"{corpus}:induced_from_model_preds" if a["supervision"] == "model_preds"
                       else f"{corpus}:induced_tau0.9")
        out.setdefault(key, []).append(m.parent)
    return out


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=ITERS)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    runs = find_runs()

    print("=" * 88)
    print(f"Document-level bootstrap, {args.iters:,} resamples, seed={SEED}")
    print("For induced conditions the MEDIAN draw is used as the representative run (D39: induction")
    print("is a distribution; the CI below is TEST-SET noise for that one guideline, not method noise).")
    print("=" * 88)
    rep: dict[str, Path] = {}
    print(f"{'condition':<34}{'K':>3}{'F1':>8}{'95% CI':>18}{'docs':>6}")
    for key in sorted(runs):
        dirs = runs[key]
        cs = [(d, f1_from(list(load_counts(d).values()))) for d in dirs]
        cs.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
        d, _ = cs[len(cs) // 2]                       # median draw
        rep[key] = d
        counts = load_counts(d)
        pt, lo, hi = boot_ci(counts, args.iters, rng)
        print(f"{key:<34}{len(dirs):>3}{pt:>8.3f}{f'[{lo:.3f}, {hi:.3f}]':>18}{len(counts):>6}")

    print("\n" + "=" * 88)
    print("PAIRED differences (same resampled documents for both sides)")
    print("=" * 88)
    pairs = [
        ("IU:induced_tau0.9", "IU:schema_only", "guideline vs no guideline (IU)"),
        ("MIMIC:induced_tau0.9", "MIMIC:schema_only", "guideline vs no guideline (MIMIC) -- THE HOOK"),
        ("IU:induced_tau0.9", "IU:human:v1_no_preamble", "induced vs the expert's own draft"),
        ("IU:induced_tau0.9", "IU:fewshot_12", "induced guideline vs 12 docs as few-shot examples"),
        ("IU:induced_tau0.9", "IU:evidence_pack", "induced guideline vs raw evidence tables"),
        ("IU:induced_tau0.9", "IU:induced_from_model_preds", "human gold vs model preds as supervision"),
    ]
    for a, b, label in pairs:
        if a not in rep or b not in rep:
            print(f"  {label:<52} -- not available yet")
            continue
        diff, lo, hi, p = boot_paired(load_counts(rep[a]), load_counts(rep[b]), args.iters, rng)
        sig = "*" if lo > 0 or hi < 0 else " "
        print(f"  {label:<52} {diff:+.3f}  95% CI [{lo:+.3f}, {hi:+.3f}]  p={p:.4f} {sig}")
    print("\n* = 95% CI excludes zero")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Map the RadGraph model's IU predictions onto OUR 50 docs' text/offsets.

Why: enables two comparisons — (a) supervised RadGraph vs our conditions on held-out 38
(D28's "vs just training a model?"), and (b) inducing a guideline from the MODEL's pilot-12
predictions instead of human gold (a clean supervision-source ablation).

The problem: RadGraph's released output uses its OWN tokenized text (spaces before punctuation)
and includes INDICATION/COMPARISON; our text is the raw report and our task is FINDINGS/IMPRESSION
only (D15). So character offsets are NOT interchangeable. We therefore:
  1. character-align RadGraph's text to ours (difflib opcodes) and translate every span offset;
  2. VERIFY each mapped span's surface text equals the original mention — drop + count if not;
  3. keep only spans inside our target sections; map ANAT-DP -> ANAT.

Output: data/interim/iu_xray/radgraph_pred.jsonl — Document-shaped (doc_id, split, text, gold=RG
spans), so it is drop-in both as an evidence source for induction and as a prediction set to score.

Usage: python scripts/ingest_radgraph_preds.py [path/to/outputs_radgraph_on_IU.zip]
"""
import json, sys, zipfile, difflib
from pathlib import Path
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
from gstudy import ingest                      # noqa: E402
from gstudy.align import target_sections       # noqa: E402
from gstudy.config import load_config          # noqa: E402
from gstudy.contracts import Document, Span    # noqa: E402

ZIP = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else \
    ROOT.parent / "original resources" / "outputs_radgraph_on_IU.zip"
LABELS = {"ANAT-DP": "ANAT", "OBS-DP": "OBS-DP", "OBS-DA": "OBS-DA", "OBS-U": "OBS-U"}

def build_index_map(src: str, dst: str) -> dict:
    """src char index -> dst char index, for characters difflib considers equal."""
    m = {}
    for tag, i1, i2, j1, j2 in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, src, dst, autojunk=False).get_opcodes():
        if tag == "equal":
            for k in range(i2 - i1):
                m[i1 + k] = j1 + k
    return m

def main():
    cfg = load_config(ROOT / "config/default.yaml")
    ours = {d.doc_id: d for d in ingest.load_jsonl(ROOT / cfg["dataset"]["interim"])}
    zf = zipfile.ZipFile(ZIP)
    names = {n.rsplit("/", 1)[-1].replace(".json", ""): n for n in zf.namelist()
             if "tateisiOrder/" in n and n.endswith(".json")}

    out, stats = [], {"docs": 0, "spans_in": 0, "mapped": 0, "verify_fail": 0,
                      "outside_sections": 0, "unknown_label": 0}
    for doc_id, d in ours.items():
        if doc_id not in names:
            print(f"WARN doc {doc_id}: no RadGraph output"); continue
        rg = json.loads(zf.read(names[doc_id]).decode("utf-8"))
        rg_text, our_text = rg["text"], d.text
        imap = build_index_map(rg_text, our_text)
        sections = target_sections(our_text)          # FINDINGS/IMPRESSION char ranges (ours)
        spans = []
        for den in rg.get("denotations", []):
            stats["spans_in"] += 1
            lab = LABELS.get(den["obj"])
            if lab is None:
                stats["unknown_label"] += 1; continue
            b, e = den["span"]["begin"], den["span"]["end"]
            if b not in imap or (e - 1) not in imap:
                stats["verify_fail"] += 1; continue
            nb, ne = imap[b], imap[e - 1] + 1
            if our_text[nb:ne] != rg_text[b:e]:       # self-check: surface must match
                stats["verify_fail"] += 1; continue
            if not any(s <= nb and ne <= t for s, t in sections):
                stats["outside_sections"] += 1; continue
            spans.append(Span(start=nb, end=ne, label=lab, text=our_text[nb:ne]))
            stats["mapped"] += 1
        out.append(Document(doc_id=doc_id, split=d.split, text=our_text, gold=spans))
        stats["docs"] += 1

    dest = ROOT / "data/interim/iu_xray/radgraph_pred.jsonl"
    ingest.write_jsonl(out, dest)
    print(json.dumps(stats, indent=2))
    print(f"wrote {dest} ({len(out)} docs, {stats['mapped']} spans)")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
